hQVTIJBZook.summary: Douglas Crockford's 2009 Google tech talk on the good and bad parts of JavaScript, based on his book. He argues for using a reliable subset of the language and avoiding its flawed features.
hQVTIJBZook.why: A classic recommended to people learning JavaScript, even though some find it dogmatic and dated.

hUhisi2FBuw.summary: Bill Hammack of Engineer Guy explains the engineering behind the aluminum beverage can: why it is cylindrical, how it is manufactured, why it narrows at the top, the double seam, and how the pull tab works.
hUhisi2FBuw.why: It is a go-to recommendation whenever cans, good design or mass-produced objects come up, and many also recommend the whole channel.

h7apO7q16V0.summary: Reducible's visual walkthrough of the Fast Fourier Transform, motivated by polynomial multiplication. It shows how the FFT's key ideas can be discovered by asking the right questions.
h7apO7q16V0.why: HN repeatedly calls it a fantastic explanation that made FFT click, with some rewatching it periodically.

hB6eY73sLV0.summary: SethBling uses Super Mario World glitches to inject and run Flappy Bird code on an unmodified SNES, entering it purely with controller inputs. It was the first time a human completed this kind of exploit by hand.
hB6eY73sLV0.why: Constantly cited as the canonical example of arbitrary code execution through gameplay and of deep system knowledge among speedrunners.

h6fcK_fRYaI.summary: Kurzgesagt animates Andy Weir's short story The Egg, in which a person learns that they are every human who has ever lived. It adds music and narration to the original text.
h6fcK_fRYaI.why: HN commenters call it a beloved story and link the animation when threads touch on consciousness, empathy or identity.

hX2aZUav-54.summary: Climate Town argues for moving away from gas stoves. It covers the gas industry's decades of marketing and lobbying, health effects of gas cooking, methane leaks, and the case for induction.
hX2aZUav-54.why: HN commenters recommend it in gas stove and induction threads for exposing how the idea that gas is better for cooking was a marketing ploy.

hxM8QmyZXtg.summary: Casey Muratori shows how fast a terminal renderer can run, building a simple reference renderer that handles Unicode and colored text far quicker than Windows Terminal. He argues that common excuses for slow terminals do not hold up.
hxM8QmyZXtg.why: It is the canonical reference for the claim that modern software wastes hardware, and the proof-of-concept behind the Windows Terminal performance debate.

hx7BXih7zx8.summary: Andrej Karpathy, then Tesla's head of AI, presents at ScaledML 2020 on how Tesla builds full self-driving using vision-based neural nets and fleet data collection. He covers training custom detectors and neural nets gradually replacing traditional code.
hx7BXih7zx8.why: HN repeatedly points to it as the best public technical overview of Tesla's FSD approach, used both to defend and to critique Tesla's progress.

hEUO6pjwFOo.summary: Robert Miles explains the orthogonality thesis: how an agent can be highly intelligent while pursuing goals that seem stupid or alien to humans. He separates intelligence from goals and touches on the stamp-collector example.
hEUO6pjwFOo.why: HN people use it as the standard short explanation for why AI can understand human ethics without sharing them, and often recommend the whole channel.

hVimVzgtD6w.summary: Hans Rosling uses the Gapminder animated-data tool to debunk myths about world development, with sportscaster-like energy. It shows trends in health, income and child survival across countries.
hVimVzgtD6w.why: HN invokes it as the classic evidence that the world has improved and that people misjudge it, and as an example of great data presentation.

hgN8pCMLI2U.summary: Bryan Cantrill's Papers We Love talk on FreeBSD Jails and Solaris Zones, tracing how OS-level virtualization grew out of chroot and the limits of the traditional UNIX security model.
hgN8pCMLI2U.why: Recommended repeatedly as the best account of container history and how Zones built on and went beyond Jails.

helScS3coAE.summary: Dave Ackley demonstrates the Demon Horde Sort, an inherently robust sorting machine running in his Movable Feast Machine simulator. This is the uncut version with all details and side thoughts.
helScS3coAE.why: HN readers recommend it as the best introduction to robust-first computing, where randomness and fault tolerance are built into the architecture.

htYh-Tq7ZBI.summary: Freya Holmer's Dutch Game Day 2023 talk asking why vectors can't be multiplied, building from complex numbers to a single axiom and arriving at geometric algebra, quaternions and multivectors.
htYh-Tq7ZBI.why: HN treats it as the best entry point to geometric algebra and an intuitive route to understanding quaternions.

hFSPHfZQpIQ.summary: Steve Blank tells how World War II, Stanford's Frederick Terman and military and intelligence agencies shaped the rise of Silicon Valley. The talk centers on the Cold War electronic warfare and signals intelligence work that seeded the region's tech industry.
hFSPHfZQpIQ.why: HN recommends it as an eye-opening, once-secret history of where Silicon Valley came from, and cites it whenever the military roots of tech come up.

huEtJw7pfLk.summary: A mashup that plays a Miles Davis improvisation video alongside an LCD Soundsystem clip with no editing, so the two seem to perform together. It also became known for an affectionate mouse cursor moving along.
huEtJw7pfLk.why: Commenters repeatedly call it a favorite and a mind-blowing introduction to jazz.

h47zZrqjgLc.summary: Bungie's David Aldridge explains the networking programming behind Halo: Reach in a 2011 GDC session. It covers how gameplay stays in sync online, including forecasting and state reconciliation.
h47zZrqjgLc.why: HN considers it one of the best game networking talks, with insights that carry over to distributed systems generally.

hER0Qp6QJNU.summary: An excerpt of Simon Sinek on Inside Quest discussing millennials in the workplace. He covers parenting, technology, social media dopamine and what that means for managers.
hER0Qp6QJNU.why: HN commenters recommend it for its take on managing young employees and on how technology and approval-seeking affect behavior.

hUyMNyrOHJQ.summary: A short video of stretching and hand exercises for preventing and easing tendinitis and carpal tunnel syndrome, from a percussion teacher. The exercises were shown to him by a doctor.
hUyMNyrOHJQ.why: Frequently recommended in RSI and wrist pain threads by people who say the stretches relieved their own symptoms.

hlrv7DIHllE.summary: Neil Postman's 1997 lecture at College of DuPage, based on his book, argues that Americans treat technology as a national religion and depend on it to solve larger human problems. It includes audience questions.
hlrv7DIHllE.why: HN recommends it to engineers as a skeptical counterweight to technology boosterism, especially for those building AI and consumer tech features.

hEx5DNLWGgA.summary: Herb Sutter's CppCon 2015 plenary on writing safe, modern C++ by default using the C++ Core Guidelines. It includes a demo of lifetime-checking static analysis tooling.
hEx5DNLWGgA.why: HN cites it in C++ versus Rust safety debates for its lifetime profile demo, and recommends it as a modern C++ talk.

hC3VTgIPoGU.summary: Footage from the Chasing Ice project of the largest glacier calving event ever filmed, at Greenland's Ilulissat Glacier in 2008. A 75-minute event is condensed to a few minutes of cameras watching ice collapse.
hC3VTgIPoGU.why: Recommended whenever glaciers come up, as a stunning look at the scale of calving.

hzyFZcuHmeI.summary: A short Healthcare Triage episode by Aaron Carroll arguing that milk gets an undeserved pass in efforts to improve diets. It examines claims about calcium and bone strength and concludes you don't need to drink milk.
hzyFZcuHmeI.why: Commenters link it as a concise evidence-based rebuttal to common beliefs about milk's health benefits.

h2I8AoB1xgU.summary: NASA's animated explanation of the Curiosity rover's Mars landing, which relied on a complex automated sequence taking about seven minutes. It features NASA engineers discussing the risks before the 2012 landing.
h2I8AoB1xgU.why: Recommended as a gripping look at how hard Mars entry, descent and landing is.

h5cm7HOAqZY.summary: Real Engineering looks at the numbers for running California on renewables, focusing on the large energy storage needed. It argues about the cost of batteries and the role of other sources.
h5cm7HOAqZY.why: Offered in energy and nuclear debates as a numbers-based walkthrough of renewable storage costs, though one commenter disliked its tone.

hMKy52Intac.summary: Ted Nelson explains the original Xanadu hypertext idea of visible connection, the notion that links between documents should be shown and preserved. He argues that the Web and current document standards lost this concept.
hMKy52Intac.why: HN commenters point to it as the author's own short explanation of Xanadu's core ideas, usually in threads on hypertext, linking and decentralizing the web.

hOE6nVVr14c.summary: Jafar Husain's ACM keynote presents Netflix's JSON Graph and Falcor, which let web developers treat all cloud data as one virtual JSON model. It combines reactive programming with REST principles.
hOE6nVVr14c.why: HN commenters point to it as an alternative take on the data-fetching problem GraphQL addresses, and as a clear argument for when RPC or graph models beat plain REST.

hdUbIlwHRkY.summary: Noam Chomsky talks with the University of Washington's Upon Reflection about how languages change over time, why a national language is a modern idea, and how language is a system of communication rooted in human nature.
hdUbIlwHRkY.why: Recommended in threads on language purity and standardization for its clear take that languages are fluid and that national languages are constructed.

hpAMbpQ8J7g.summary: An RSA Animate adaptation of a Slavoj Zizek talk on charitable giving and ethical consumerism. It argues that buying products that bundle a charity donation can sustain the system that causes the problems.
hpAMbpQ8J7g.why: Frequently linked in threads on philanthropy, ethical consumption and billionaire giving as a short, approachable critique of charity.

hpgK51w6uhk.summary: Machine Thinking tells the story of the Cold War Heavy Press Program, the giant forging presses that make parts for aircraft, missiles and turbines.
hpgK51w6uhk.why: HN commenters recommend it as an excellent introduction to massive forging presses, especially in threads about gigacasting and large manufacturing machines.

hs3piaN4b5I.summary: Jen Simmons explains the difference between CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid, and when to use each. She makes the case that Grid does not replace Flexbox and most sites use both.
hs3piaN4b5I.why: Recommended as a short, clear rundown of one-dimensional versus two-dimensional layout.

hvk_XylEmLo.summary: Historia Civilis traces the history of work and time discipline, comparing modern working hours with those of medieval peasants and the changes brought by clocks and industrialization. It draws on works such as Schor's The Overworked American.
hvk_XylEmLo.why: HN uses it in work-hours and four-day-week threads as the source for the claim that people worked fewer hours before the industrial era.

hz_mMLhUinw.summary: Technology Connections explains why the superheterodyne radio has its name and how mixing frequencies lets it tune stations well. It walks through the underlying wave phenomena and algebra and why the design solved a hard tuning problem.
hz_mMLhUinw.why: HN people use it as the accessible go-to explainer for the superhet trick whenever radios or signal processing come up.

h3gwyHNo7MI.summary: The first episode of Adam Curtis's 1992 BBC series Pandora's Box, on the engineers' plot, examining communism in the Soviet Union and the rise and limits of technocratic central planning.
h3gwyHNo7MI.why: HN recommends it as a fun, well-made documentary on Soviet planning, Gosplan, and why central control failed.

h4Uu5eyN6VU.summary: Kurzgesagt explains how the European Union is governed, how its officials are elected or appointed, and whether a citizen's vote actually matters.
h4Uu5eyN6VU.why: HN commenters point to it as a quick factual primer on EU institutions when threads get into EU politics and policy.

hFL6qRIJZ_Y.summary: Andrew Huberman discusses ADHD, its biology and myths, behavioral and pharmacologic treatments, and training protocols to improve focus for people with or without ADHD. It covers dopamine and the coordination of brain networks.
hFL6qRIJZ_Y.why: HN people offer it as practical focus and ADHD advice from a credentialed neuroscientist, though some treat it as only a reference.

hXgqik6HXc0.summary: Clip from Lex Fridman's podcast with Roger Penrose in which Penrose argues that consciousness is not a computation. He discusses Godel-style arguments and the possible role of quantum effects in microtubules.
hXgqik6HXc0.why: Pointed to in consciousness and AI threads as the best-known statement of Penrose's view, which commenters find interesting even when they disagree.

ho7oagHeqNc.summary: Eugenia Cheng gives the opening keynote at Lambda World 2017, presenting category theory as very abstract algebra whose abstraction gives it broad applicability. She applies it to everyday questions including privilege and prejudice.
ho7oagHeqNc.why: HN recommends it as an accessible, gentle introduction that makes category theory feel approachable and shows its analogy-making power.

hzPd3umu78g.summary: Aaron Hsu shows how to manipulate and transform tree data in APL using arrays and inverted tables instead of pointers. He claims much smaller code, better performance and easier parallelisation.
hzPd3umu78g.why: HN recommends it as a striking example of high-performance tree handling with array programming.

hCQCP-5g5bo.summary: Benn Jordan's video about storing a PNG image in a living bird, a starling that learns to reproduce encoded sounds. It mixes ornithology, audio engineering, and data encoding.
hCQCP-5g5bo.why: HN fans point to it as a fun, nerdy crossover of bird song acoustics and technology, and the story itself got its own thread.

hIZxTQP1ifo.summary: Edward Kmett speaks at the Boston Haskell meetup about type classes and the design tradeoffs of global coherence compared with other approaches to implicit instances. It covers why uniqueness of instances matters for reasoning and refactoring.
hIZxTQP1ifo.why: HN points to it as the definitive explanation of why coherence and the orphan rule matter, in debates over Haskell, Rust traits, OCaml modules and Elm.

hckwxq8rnr0.summary: CuriousMarc's Apollo Guidance Computer restoration series looks at core rope memory, the ROM that held the Moon landing programs. Mike Stewart builds a custom reader to recover lost AGC programs.
hckwxq8rnr0.why: HN commenters recommend it as the deepest explanation of how AGC rope memory works and how it differs from core memory.

hhMAt3BluAU.summary: A long video essay by Kraut arguing that Trump's biggest failure was his handling of China. It spends much of its length on Chinese history, culture, the trade war, and the rise of a communist superpower.
hhMAt3BluAU.why: Commenters point to it as a well-researched explainer of the history and culture behind China's current position, despite the political title.

hk-0qJXyido.summary: Anders Puck Nielsen analyzes the Nord Stream pipeline sabotage using Kilcullen's theory of liminal warfare and prospect theory. He argues from the operational design that Russia is the most likely culprit, then discusses how hybrid warfare might be used against Europe.
hk-0qJXyido.why: HN points to it as a compact, reasoned case for Russian responsibility, though at least one commenter found the argument unconvincing.

hyYCn_kAngI.summary: A Startup School talk by YC partner and former Airbnb growth head Gustaf Alstromer on how startups get their first customers. It covers doing things that don't scale, founders learning sales, the sales funnel, and charging your first customer.
hyYCn_kAngI.why: Commenters recommend the whole talk as practical, tactical advice for early customer acquisition and outbound sales.

h2cs8QLnxlU.summary: Part one of Sergey Kuryokhin's 1991 live Soviet TV hoax in which he claimed that Lenin was a mushroom. With subtitles, it shows how a surreal absurd theory can be made to seem proven on live television.
h2cs8QLnxlU.why: Shared as a delightful example of a famous media hoax.

h67k9eEw9AY.summary: A George Carlin stand-up bit from Doin' It Again about soft language and euphemism, showing how softened words hide uncomfortable facts. It touches on topics like shell shock and aging.
h67k9eEw9AY.why: Cited whenever euphemisms appear in corporate, product or news language, as the classic comedic critique.

h7Sv_pS8MgQ.summary: MedCram's Dr. Roger Seheult summarizes a discussion with Dr. Michael Mina on cheap, paper-based at-home COVID-19 antigen tests. It explains why lower sensitivity can still work well for screening infectious people.
h7Sv_pS8MgQ.why: Pointed to in 2020 testing threads for a visual explanation of why rapid antigen tests still serve a purpose.

hBmhDf8cl0k.summary: A demonstration of Larynx, an offline open source neural text-to-speech system supporting nine languages. The video itself is narrated with a Larynx-generated voice.
hBmhDf8cl0k.why: HN points to it as proof that offline TTS can sound natural, relevant to private voice assistant alternatives.

hBpetDxIEMU.summary: Steven Pinker presents his book The Stuff of Thought at Google in 2007. He covers language as a window into human nature, including taboo words, swearing and the psychology and game theory of indirect speech like bribery.
hBpetDxIEMU.why: HN commenters cite it for Pinker's analysis of profanity and of why talking about taboo words differs from using them.

hJP5GqnTrNo.summary: Sal Khan of Khan Academy gives a TED talk on how AI could transform education, with a personal tutor for every student and a teaching assistant for every teacher. He demos Khanmigo, including features where the AI reasons before responding.
hJP5GqnTrNo.why: Cited in AI-and-education threads as the optimistic case and demo for AI tutoring, and as a source on Khan Academy's LLM approach.

hMOwbNUpDQA.summary: Andreas Spiess explains the basic principles of LoRa and LoRaWAN, their pros and cons, link budget and bandwidth. He shows his own gateway and client sending a message to The Things Network.
hMOwbNUpDQA.why: Recommended as a clear introduction to LoRa and the link budget idea that sets it apart.

hSrGfElyfVE.summary: Footage of FAA altitude chamber hypoxia training for pilots in which a participant passes out from oxygen deprivation. It shows how quickly and subtly cognition fails at altitude.
hSrGfElyfVE.why: Linked as a vivid demonstration of how fast hypoxia incapacitates people, often without them noticing.

hT8GZlBBv5k.summary: Medlife Crisis examines why some elite endurance athletes die in their sleep, covering extremely slow heart rates and the effects of performance-enhancing drugs that thicken blood. It uses cyclist Marco Pantani as an example.
hT8GZlBBv5k.why: HN recommends it as a good, short explanation of athlete's heart and the risks of extreme fitness.

hZ1OgQL9_Cw.summary: Footage shot in New York City in 1911 by a Swedish film company, upscaled to 4K and 60 fps with neural networks and optionally colorized. The creator notes the colors are artificial and added only for ambiance.
hZ1OgQL9_Cw.why: HN points to it as an impressive example of ML-based video restoration, and as the test case in the debate over whether upscaling historical footage is respectful or misleading.

hdt18p-VMmQ.summary: William Osman describes helping build parts of the MrBeast Squid Game event, including hacking together hundreds of wifi-controlled blood packs in about three weeks. He covers the chaos and near-failures along the way.
hdt18p-VMmQ.why: Makers recommend it as a behind-the-scenes look at crunch-time hardware engineering for a big YouTube production.

hhiLw5Q_UFg.summary: UC Berkeley EECS colloquium by OpenAI's John Schulman on reinforcement learning from human feedback. He covers why RL helps with truthfulness, hallucination, and the limits of behavior cloning.
hhiLw5Q_UFg.why: Recommended in LLM threads as an authoritative explanation from a ChatGPT architect of why models hallucinate and why imitation is not enough.

hyry8mgXiTk.summary: Eric Cline presents the thesis of his book 1177 BC on the collapse of the interconnected Late Bronze Age Mediterranean civilizations. The talk covers the Egyptians, Mycenaeans, Hittites, Canaanites and their trade networks.
hyry8mgXiTk.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining intro to the Bronze Age collapse from the book's author.

hzGaO4Kdz2Y.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog tears down a Kollsman MD-1 Automatic Astro Compass, a mechanical analog computer from a B-52 bomber. It is part of a star-tracker inertial navigation system that computes altitude and azimuth.
hzGaO4Kdz2Y.why: Pointed to when people want to see the cams and gears inside a mechanical navigation computer.

hMtu7vV_HmY.summary: Dan Tentler shows a rapid-fire tour of insecure things found on the open internet using Shodan and his own scanning, from unprotected VNC endpoints to industrial controls. The emphasis is on how little security was considered before connecting them.
hMtu7vV_HmY.why: HN points to it as an entertaining, jaw-dropping demonstration of exposed systems, including a French dam's controls.

hNRO7lno_DM.summary: The winning demo from Revision 2015's oldskool competition, running on a real 1981 IBM PC with CGA at 4.77MHz. It uses extreme tricks to produce effects, graphics and sound far beyond what the hardware was thought capable of.
hNRO7lno_DM.why: Held up as the peak of demoscene hardware hacking, especially for its finale and for how good the PC speaker sound gets.

hWLjYJ4BzvI.summary: A short compilation of dozens of local news anchors at Sinclair-owned stations reading the same scripted promo about biased and fake news. It went viral in 2018 as an example of centralized media messaging.
hWLjYJ4BzvI.why: Cited as an example of media consolidation and coordinated messaging, mostly in threads about distrust of news, though it is also posted as a plain source.

hWUiLJnEYJI.summary: The earliest existing concert video of Kraftwerk, from a 1970 performance shortly after the band formed. It shows the band in its original setup and the audience's reactions.
hWUiLJnEYJI.why: Used in techno-history threads as evidence of Kraftwerk's role in the genre's origins and as an example of original work.

h_zgURwr6nA.summary: ASML's short promotional fly-through of its High NA EUV lithography platform, the TWINSCAN EXE, which supports 8-nanometer resolution. It shows the machine's internals including advanced anamorphic optics.
h_zgURwr6nA.why: HN links it to show the sheer complexity of EUV machines, especially when discussing whether competitors can challenge ASML.

h4T_LlK1VE4.summary: Mark Rober builds a third-generation glitter bomb trap and films it catching package thieves, with phone trackers and fart spray included. It shows the engineering behind the build and the comic payoff.
h4T_LlK1VE4.why: Cited in porch-pirate threads as the definitive revenge-engineering project, praised for its impressive engineering.

h6MfM8EFkGg.summary: The Signal Path takes apart a Starlink dish layer by layer, analyzing the phased array RF design, system architecture and integrated circuits, with an X-ray of the RF stack.
h6MfM8EFkGg.why: Recommended as the deep, expert RF analysis behind Starlink's hardware.

hBMoPUAeLnY.summary: A roughly three-hour Joe Rogan interview with Donald Trump during the 2024 campaign. It covers policy topics including tariffs and taxes.
hBMoPUAeLnY.why: Cited as a primary source for Trump's own stated positions, such as replacing income tax with tariffs.

hE2lna5Wxuo.summary: Casey Neistat's short New York Times op-doc investigating how accurate restaurant and packaged-food calorie labels really are. He gets items from chains like Chipotle, Starbucks and Subway measured by nutrition researchers and compares them to the printed numbers.
hE2lna5Wxuo.why: Cited in threads on calorie counting as a quick, visual demonstration that labeled calories can be well off.

hKcOkWzj0_s.summary: Yaron Minsky explains how Jane Street moved from mainstream languages to developing almost entirely in OCaml. He covers trading systems, research infrastructure, tooling and hiring.
hKcOkWzj0_s.why: Cited as evidence for OCaml's readability benefits and for hiring in less popular languages.

hKqVvXTanzI.summary: Linus Tech Tips looks at whether buying a used GPU that was previously used for crypto mining is a good idea, as miners prepare to sell off cards. The video discusses how mining affects wear on cards and what to watch for.
hKqVvXTanzI.why: HN cites it as evidence that mining does not meaningfully degrade GPUs, so used mining cards are generally fine buys.

hLrFyjGZ9NU.summary: A Vox Borders explainer on Hong Kong's housing crisis, the least affordable market in the world, and the tiny cage homes and subdivided flats people squeeze into. It looks at why prices keep climbing and how land policy contributes.
hLrFyjGZ9NU.why: Cited in housing and real estate threads as a vivid illustration of extreme scarcity and Hong Kong's land-price dynamics.

hM_h0UA7upI.summary: A No Priors podcast conversation with Andrej Karpathy covering self-driving (Tesla versus Waymo), the Optimus robot, bottlenecks in AI development, and his education project Eureka Labs.
hM_h0UA7upI.why: Commenters cite it for Karpathy's views on Tesla versus Waymo, neural networks as a path to AGI, and the quality of internet data for LLMs.

hNDgcjVGHIw.summary: NYT Opinion video essay arguing that Democrat-controlled states like California, New York and Illinois often fall short of their egalitarian values. It focuses on housing costs, homelessness, regressive taxes and school segregation as drivers of inequality.
hNDgcjVGHIw.why: Brought up in housing and zoning threads as a mainstream outlet making the case that progressive NIMBYism contradicts stated values.

hQ58Yv6kP44.summary: Vladimir Putin's February 2007 speech at the Munich Security Conference, criticizing a unipolar world and US use of force and NATO expansion. This upload presents the full speech with a sympathetic framing.
hQ58Yv6kP44.why: HN cites it as a primary source for Russia's grievances over NATO expansion, mostly in threads about Ukraine.

hSyfZkVgasI.summary: A one-minute clip about Paul Otlet, the Belgian bibliographer who in 1934 imagined users accessing a remote database through an electric telescope over a phone line. It presents his vision as a precursor of the web.
hSyfZkVgasI.why: Brought up whenever early predictions of the internet and the web's origins are discussed.

hTsrDpsYHrw.summary: Fully Charged episode where Elliot drives the NIO ES8 SUV and visits a battery swap station that replaces the pack in about three minutes. It covers the ownership model of swapping and what it could mean for EV charging.
hTsrDpsYHrw.why: Linked as concrete evidence that automated battery swapping already works in practice, especially in China.

hV41QEKiMlM.summary: Freeman Dyson recounts how Enrico Fermi rejected his team's meson scattering model, noting that it had too many free parameters. It is the source of the quote about fitting an elephant.
hV41QEKiMlM.why: Cited in modeling and machine learning threads as the classic story on overfitting and justifying parameters.

hWTFG3J1CP8.summary: A song by Pig With The Face Of A Boy that narrates the history of the Soviet Union from a worker's view, set to the Tetris melody.
hWTFG3J1CP8.why: HN posts it as a clever, catchy musical joke whenever Tetris or Soviet history comes up.

hZRL8luuPb8.summary: The 8-Bit Guy explains how character LCD screens work and how to control them directly, first part of a series.
hZRL8luuPb8.why: HN commenters recommend the series as an approachable demonstration of the simple standardized interface used by character LCDs.

hcGgaa2mFc4.summary: Royal Institution lecture by Dr Kate Lancaster on the most powerful lasers in the world and the extreme conditions they create. It includes live demonstrations and covers applications from industry to fusion.
hcGgaa2mFc4.why: Recommended as an accessible, well-delivered lecture on high-intensity laser physics.

hcRxFRgNpns.summary: Stanford Blitzscaling class session where Reid Hoffman interviews Eric Schmidt about structuring teams and scaling Google. Topics include Alphabet, hiring, and how Chrome and Android operated inside the company.
hcRxFRgNpns.why: Cited as a first-hand source for how Google's leadership thought about hiring, organization and the Alphabet restructuring.

hfQdf93e63I.summary: RedLetterMedia's Mike and Rich review the first episode of Star Trek: Picard. It is a long, jokey and critical take from long-time Star Trek fans.
hfQdf93e63I.why: Cited as an entertaining and brutal review of Picard, including in a thread about a takedown of another Picard review.

hksVvXONrIo.summary: A short video arguing that the iPhone keyboard has gotten worse, showing slow-motion footage of taps registering the wrong letters. It claims the problem is iOS itself rather than user error.
hksVvXONrIo.why: Linked repeatedly as clear evidence of the iOS keyboard bug when people complain about typos.

hoTxiRWrvp8.summary: A Vox explainer on how many of the British Museum's treasures were taken during British imperial rule, focusing on the Benin Bronzes and requests for their return.
hoTxiRWrvp8.why: Cited as an accessible overview of the looted-artifacts debate around the British Museum.

hpTCZ-hO6iI.summary: A 60 Minutes Australia segment on people with highly superior autobiographical memory, who can recall the details of any day of their lives. It presents the rare phenomenon through interviews with people who have it.
hpTCZ-hO6iI.why: HN links it as an example of extraordinary episodic memory in threads on memory and knowledge.

hps-HfpL1vc.summary: Astrophysicist Dr. Becky explains the Hubble tension, the disagreement between expansion-rate measurements from the cosmic microwave background and the distance ladder, and what early JWST Cepheid observations add.
hps-HfpL1vc.why: Recommended as an accessible layperson introduction to the Hubble tension when new expansion-rate results make the news.

hsIpQ7YguGE.summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman arguing with students that equal pay laws are counterproductive, and that markets penalize discrimination because cheaper equally productive workers are an advantage to hire.
hsIpQ7YguGE.why: Cited in debates over pay equity law as Friedman's free-market argument on discrimination.

hyCIpKAIFyo.summary: 'Pipe Dream' is the best-known piece from the first Animusic DVD, a computer-animated music video in which fantastical machines play music. The animation is driven by MIDI data.
hyCIpKAIFyo.why: HN people bring it up whenever music-playing machines or robot bands come up, as the classic CG precursor.

h0962biiZa4.summary: A panel from the Beneficial AI 2017 conference moderated by Max Tegmark, with Elon Musk, Stuart Russell, Kurzweil, Hassabis, Harris, Bostrom, Chalmers and others. They discuss likely outcomes of human-level AGI and what outcomes are desirable.
h0962biiZa4.why: HN mostly cites it for specific statements, such as Hassabis on AGI and safety buffers, rather than recommending it outright.

h2OfQdYrHRs.summary: A one-minute demo of Word Lens, an iPhone app that translates printed text in real time by overlaying the translation on the camera view. It was later folded into Google Translate.
h2OfQdYrHRs.why: HN brings it up as an early, impressive augmented-reality translation demo and a wow moment before modern AI.

h5d82ndui_s.summary: A two-minute clip from The Wire in which characters work through the meaning of the word evacuate, an exchange that has become a meme.
h5d82ndui_s.why: HN uses it purely as a joke reply when an evacuation or similar wording comes up.

h5gnATQMtPg.summary: A talk by Eric Weinstein on gauge theory and its possible application to economics and inflation. It proposes extending the Wu-Yang dictionary into a geometric tool beyond physics.
h5gnATQMtPg.why: Cited mainly as the available video of Weinstein's gauge-theory-of-economics ideas, sometimes skeptically.

hE7k0_9k0VA.summary: Peter Norvig answers the top questions submitted by reddit users in a 27-minute interview. Topics include programming language choice, AI, and workplace design.
hE7k0_9k0VA.why: HN mostly quotes it for specific Norvig remarks, such as language choice mattering less and the open-space versus cubicle trade-off.

hGo5bxWy21g.summary: A short clip from The Wire, season 3, in which Stringer Bell chairs a meeting of the New Day Co-Op with Prop Joe and Fat-Face Rick. The scene shows the drug crews running their cooperative like a formal business meeting.
hGo5bxWy21g.why: HN uses it as a joke reference, posting it in threads about meetings, procedure and corporate behavior.

hIXhnWUmMvw.summary: A VPRO documentary in which Harvard professor Shoshana Zuboff explains her book on surveillance capitalism. It covers how Google and Facebook turn personal data into raw material for prediction and behavioral influence.
hIXhnWUmMvw.why: Linked as a reference in privacy and big tech threads for framing the business model of data extraction.

hNZy603as5w.summary: Tom Scott borrows a Nio electric car in China and shows its automated battery swap station replacing the whole battery in minutes. He explains how swapping serves as an alternative to charging.
hNZy603as5w.why: Go-to reference in EV threads for showing that battery swapping already works in practice.

hNoS2BU6bbQ.summary: A classic sketch from A Bit of Fry and Laurie in which a man at a police station has a surname that is very hard to pronounce. Stephen Fry and Hugh Laurie play it out as a comic exchange.
hNoS2BU6bbQ.why: HN brings it up as a joke whenever threads touch on long names, name handling or unpronounceable identifiers.

hNuu9CpdjIo.summary: A short clip from the film Office Space in which Tom Smykowski insists he has people skills. It is a well-known workplace comedy scene.
hNuu9CpdjIo.why: HN uses it as a recurring joke about people skills, managers and CEOs, and about the value of non-technical skills in tech.

hOSYiT2iG08.summary: A Blackadder the Third scene in which Dr Johnson delivers his dictionary, which lacks Blackadder's invented insults such as contrafibularity.
hOSYiT2iG08.why: HN quotes it as a joke in threads about made-up words and vocabulary.

hShY6xZWVGE.summary: A short clip from Star Trek IV in which Scotty tries to talk to a 20th-century computer, picks up the mouse and says 'Hello, computer'.
hShY6xZWVGE.why: HN uses it as a joke in threads about voice interfaces and talking to computers.

hSp8IyaKCs0.summary: A short George Carlin routine on how the term shell shock was softened into combat fatigue and then PTSD. He argues that euphemism hides the reality of suffering.
hSp8IyaKCs0.why: It is cited in debates about euphemism and language policing, usually by commenters who think softer terms change nothing.

hV-05TLiiLU.summary: A short clip of Nancy Pelosi saying Congress has to pass the health care bill so people can find out what is in it. It circulated widely in debates over the Affordable Care Act.
hV-05TLiiLU.why: Used critically as a shorthand quote when commenters complain about legislation passed without being read.

hWiBt-pqp0E.summary: A George Carlin stand-up routine arguing that rights are really temporary privileges that can be taken away. The uploader frames it with conspiracy-leaning tags.
hWiBt-pqp0E.why: HN quotes it in threads about civil liberties and government overreach for its line about rights being privileges.

hX1YVzdnpEc.summary: A 2012 parody dub that splices clips of Barack Obama speaking into a performance of Carly Rae Jepsen's 'Call Me Maybe'. It is a short comedic mashup built entirely from re-ordered snippets of his real speech.
hX1YVzdnpEc.why: HN commenters cite it as a silly but clear example of how cutting and reordering real footage can fabricate meaning without any deepfake technology.

hYAuR5bkIlQ.summary: A short Simpsons clip (S5E20) of the 'Am I so out of touch?' moment, in which Principal Skinner concludes it must be the children who are wrong.
hYAuR5bkIlQ.why: Used as a meme reply when someone's view clashes with everyone else's.

hgOzYZDrXL0.summary: Lennart Augustsson's CUFP 2011 keynote covers using Haskell commercially at Standard Chartered Bank. He discusses non-standard Haskell implementations, including a strict dialect, and weighs strict against lazy evaluation.
hgOzYZDrXL0.why: It is the reference for Mu, Standard Chartered's strict Haskell, and for the practical case that strictness makes debugging easier.

hkDD03yeLnU.summary: A short CSI clip in which characters try to track a killer's IP address by writing a Visual Basic GUI. It is a famous example of absurd TV hacking.
hkDD03yeLnU.why: Used as a running joke whenever HN discusses Hollywood hacking or nonsense technical jargon.

hlmf032NmHU.summary: Cleared Defense Department footage of Raytheon's Phaser high-power microwave weapon bringing down drones during a 2013 live-fire demonstration at Fort Sill. Raytheon says it has halved the payload size and is offering the system for operational use.
hlmf032NmHU.why: HN cites it as evidence that microwave and electromagnetic weapons against drones are real and already tested.

hnOPu0_YWhw.summary: Washington Post video of the experiment in which violinist Joshua Bell played incognito at a D.C. metro station. It asks whether commuters would notice a world-class musician in an ordinary setting.
hnOPu0_YWhw.why: Referenced in threads on busking, art perception and context as the standard example of great work going unnoticed.

hou0lU8WMgo.summary: The Futurama clip where Hermes is told he is technically correct, the best kind of correct. It comes from season 2, episode 14.
hou0lU8WMgo.why: Posted as a joke reply when someone makes a pedantic but technically accurate point.
